newsitem.title: RUSSIA: RUSSIA'S ORIENT-AVIA MAY LOSE OPERATING LICENCE.
newsitem.headline: RUSSIA'S ORIENT-AVIA MAY LOSE OPERATING LICENCE.

text.p: Russia's Federal Aviation Service (FAS) is considering cancelling the licence for air operations of private airline AO Orient-Avia, a FAS official said on Monday.
The official, who asked not to be named, told Reuters FAS would announce a decision later this week.
Orient-Avia officials could not be contacted for comment.
But another Russian civil aviation official said four long-range Orient-Avia aircraft had been arrested in Russian airports after the company cancelled regular passenger flights on June 10.
"Four Ilyushin Il-62 jets are arrested at Vladivostok and Moscow's Sheremetyevo and Domodedovo airports," he said.

Last month, an Orient-Avia spokeswoman said the company had cancelled all scheduled flights from Moscow to Vladivostok and Petropavlovsk-Kamchatsky as well as booking and selling tickets to these flights. She declined to say why the airline was in difficulties.
Orient-Avia has not flown since then.
Moscow-based carrier Domodedovo Airlines was carrying some of Orient-Avia's stranded passengers between Moscow and Petropavlovsk and Vladivostok and Aeroflot joined this operation later.
"We carry these passengers... but we do not know who will pay us for it," Aeroflot's domestic flights department deputy head Leonid Mokhov said.
The FAS said about 1,500 Orient-Avia tickets had been sold on flights booked between July 10 and August 31.
Orient-Avia, set up in 1994, carried 161,000 passengers and 1,560 tonnes of cargo and mail in 1996.

In June Orient-Avia and East Line Air announced they had merged to create a new airline, East Line Aviation, headed by Orient-Avia's chief executive Amiran Kurtanidze. Officials from East Line Air and the new merged airline were not available for comment.
